text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed higher on the strength of New York arabica prices but conditions were subdued. July closed $12 higher at $1,585 per tonne, while September added $25 to close at $1,615 per tonne. July 31 is the last trading and delivery day for the spot July contract.

On the physical front, Indonesian coffee prices continued to firm on the back of tight local supply. Elsewhere warm, high pressure over Brazil's coffee belt is expected to remain in place for the next seven days, preventing any cold air from moving into the area.

Arabica futures in New York closed sharply higher, particularly in the spot September contract on continued concerns about the lack of deliverable supplies available against the September position and the unlikelihood that any fresh coffee will become available to satisfy these requirements.

With little certifiable coffee expected to make its way to the exchange ahead of the autumn harvest of many new-crop Latin American coffees, a draw down of certified coffee stocks going into the September delivery period must be expected. Traders said September is the most squeezable month because its delivery is ahead of the Colombian main crop and there is nothing out of Central America.

Additionally, traders noted that more than half of the coffee recently graded failed to pass CSCE approval and there has been talk that some members of the trade were unhappy with the quality of some certified coffee stocks from Africa. September added 12.05 cents/lb to close at 188.35 cents/lb. December closed 7.15 cents/lb higher at 164.40 cents/lb.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks fell by 750 bags on July 25 to 92,078 bags, down from 92,828 bags the previous day and 90,645 bags on July 23. There were 2,367 bags pending grading on July 25.

MEXICO - According to the Mexican Coffee Council, coffee production in 1996/97 (October/September) reached 5.1 million 60- kg bags, of which 4,921,500 bags arabicas and 178,500 robustas. This compares to 5,211,000 and 189,000 bags respectively in 1995/96.

JAPAN - Japan imported 534,300 bags of green coffee in June 1997, which compares to 488,617 bags imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports of green coffee since the beginning of 1997 up to 3.047 million bags, 19 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Main suppliers of green coffee in June 1997 were Brazil (113,017 vs 69,267 bags), Colombia (87,533 vs 81,667 bags) and Indonesia (106,850 vs 90,200 bags).
